sections.title: Roof repair for Mission homes
paras: Mission is a younger city than most people think. About half of its homes were built in 2000 or later, and the median home was built in 2000, according to Census Bureau survey data (ACS 2020 to 2024). Around 68% are single family houses. So a lot of Mission roofs are still the original roof, put on when the house was built, and many of those are now 20 years old or more.

In the Valley, a shingle roof that age is close to worn out. The shingles get brittle, the granules wash into the gutters, and the sealant around vents and flashing dries out. That is when the small leaks start. A small leak on an older roof is still usually a repair, as long as the rest of the roof is sound.
We come to Mission from our office at 1815 N Jackson Rd in Edinburg. It is about 17 miles, roughly 26 minutes to Mission City Hall.

sections.title: Hail and heavy rain in Mission
paras: Mission sits in the path of the spring storms that cross the Valley. On April 21, 2023, spotters reported hail up to 2.5 inches in Mission and 2.75 inches in Peñitas, according to National Weather Service storm reports. On May 29, 2023, hail near 0.88 inches fell about a mile east of town. Hail that size cracks shingles and knocks off the granules that protect them from the sun.

Rain is the other test. Hurricane Hanna dropped 14.40 inches of rain on Mission in July 2020, and the NWS reported hundreds of poorly built homes and other buildings damaged, mostly roofs. At the McAllen airport, the closest official weather station, September is the wettest month at about 4.6 inches (NOAA 1991 to 2020 normals). A roof that starts leaking slowly in spring often shows up as a ceiling stain by fall.

cards.title: Hail damaged shingles
cards.body: We replace cracked or bruised shingles where the hail hit and match them to your roof as close as we can. You get the damage in writing for your insurance company.

cards.title: Aging flashing
cards.body: On a 20 year old roof, the sealant at walls and valleys has dried out. We reseal or replace the flashing so water runs off again.

cards.title: Vent and pipe boots
cards.body: Rubber boots around plumbing vents crack in the sun. Replacing one is quick and stops a leak that is easy to miss.

cards.title: Leaks after heavy rain
cards.body: We trace the water back to where it enters the roof, which is often a few feet from where it drips inside.

cards.title: Missing shingles
cards.body: Shingles torn off by wind get replaced, and we check the ones around them for broken seals.

cards.title: Soft decking
cards.body: If a slow leak has softened the wood under the shingles, that section of decking is replaced before the roof is closed back up.

sections.title: Repair or replace a 20 year old Mission roof?
paras: If the leak is in one place and the shingles around it still bend without cracking, a repair makes sense. If the roof leaks in several places, has bare patches where the granules are gone, or has soft decking in more than one area, the money is better spent on a new roof. We tell you which one we see and show you the photos, so you can decide for yourself.

If you are leaning toward a new roof, read about roof replacement in Mission. For claims after a storm, see storm and hail damage in Mission. Our post on roof repair cost in Mission goes deeper on pricing and insurance.

sections.title: Roof repair questions from Mission homeowners

faqs.q: What is a fair price for a roof repair in Mission?
faqs.a: Most repairs fall between a few hundred dollars and about $1,500. Where yours lands depends on what failed and how big the area is. We can't give you a fair number over the phone. We write the estimate after we see the roof and before we start.

faqs.q: My roof is over 20 years old. Will my insurance still cover it?
faqs.a: The Texas Department of Insurance says insurers cannot refuse or drop a policy because of roof age alone, but they can look at the roof's condition. Some policies switch older roofs to actual cash value, which pays less after depreciation. Read your policy, and call your agent if you are not sure. A written inspection report helps either way.

faqs.q: Do I need a windstorm inspection for my Mission roof?
faqs.a: Not for TWIA. Hidalgo County is not one of the 14 coastal counties in the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association area, so a TDI windstorm certificate is not needed for TWIA eligibility. The city does require an engineered, sealed windstorm plan when you permit a new house.

faqs.q: Does a roof repair need a permit in Mission?
faqs.a: Mission's residential permit application does not spell out roof repairs. Call the city's Inspections Division at (956) 580-8691 to check your job. Under the city's rules, work done without a required permit pays a double fee, so the call is worth it.

faqs.q: How soon can you get to Mission?
faqs.a: We are about 26 minutes away. After a big storm a lot of people call at once, so call early and we will give you a time.

faqs.q: How do I get a repair estimate in Mission?
faqs.a: Call (956) 422-3335 or book an inspection online. It is free, and there is no obligation.
